# invest.stock.db

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of invest.stock.db is to support the creation of a structured database for stock data to facilitate investment analysis.
It also provides a set of functions to calculate common financial metrics and indicators on the data stored in the database. 

## Installation

This package is still in development, and is highly linked to a second package: "invest.data". The invest.data package is responsible for getting the data from different sources and providing it in a structured format, while the invest.stock.db package is responsible for creating the database and populating it with the data provided by invest.data. Therefore, to use invest.stock.db, you will also need to install invest.data.

You can install the development version of both packages from GitHub:

``` r
# install.packages("remotes") # if you don't have it already
# dependencies = TRUE will install all the packages needed to run the functions in invest.stock.db, 
# and build_vignettes = TRUE will build the vignettes so you can access them after installing the package.
remotes::install_github("henrique-anatole/invest.data", dependencies = TRUE, build_vignettes = TRUE)
remotes::install_github("henrique-anatole/invest.stock.db", dependencies = TRUE, build_vignettes = TRUE)

```

## Step by step example

A step by step on how to create a new stock price database can be checked in the vignette "my_new_stock_db". 
You can clone a project implementing it here: https://github.com/henrique-anatole/stock_data_db
``` r
browseVignettes("invest.stock.db")

```

## Transform the data to get indicators and other metrics

``` r
browseVignettes("add_indicators")
```
